summary: FD_TC_080_No Travel Origin, Required for Safety (fallback: departure delay code 44, spares and maintenance equipment), APPR, Basic Aeroplan
title: No Travel Origin, Required for Safety (fallback: departure delay code 44, spares and maintenance equipment), APPR, Basic Aeroplan
description:
A single-leg flight is delayed more than 3 hours. There's no cancellation code and no arrival delay code, so the rules engine falls back to the first departure delay code, 44. A required replacement part wasn't in stock at YUL and had to be flown in before the aircraft could safely depart (within carrier's control but required for safety). The customer chose not to travel and stayed at the origin. Checks that the fallback path is used, that DDS classes code 44 as Safety and returns NE-15 (no cash compensation, expenses plus full refund entitlement), and that the linked Aeroplan Basic profile (tier A) is shown but doesn't change the outcome.

Prerequisites:
PNR TC068: one adult passenger, �mile Gagnon. One AC domestic leg: AC 470, YUL?YYZ, May 31, 2026. Scheduled 10:00 ? 12:00. Actual departure 14:15 (255 min late). Actual arrival 16:20 (260 min late). Status: DELAYED (operated). Cancellation code: NONE. Arrival delay code: NOT AVAILABLE (null/empty). First departure delay code 44 (TS). No other delay codes on the MSL. Part shortage at YUL on the operating aircraft, not upline. Passenger not boarded, coupon not flown. Customer stayed at YUL. No Travel status: Origin. No rebooking accepted. Aeroplan: linked, tier code A (Aeroplan Basic). No expense receipts. Fallback: TRUE. Regime: APPR. More than 72 hours have passed. Filed within 366 days.
